title: macos-latest Test step wedges to the 20-minute job timeout on main pushes (evidence for a pending decision)
description: EVIDENCE ONLY; carrier for a decision opum-doc is taking. No ci.yml change and no fix until it returns. Job "lint . typecheck . test (macos-latest)", step "Test". Every wedge is a cancel at the job timeout-minutes: 20 (~20m20s), never a test failure. LEADER-MEASURED 2026-10-23 ~00:55Z: across 43 macOS job attempts on the last 40 main-push CI runs, 13 timeout wedges, 2 failures, 28 successes; since 2026-10-06, 9 wedges in 20 attempts; earliest wedge in that window is run 36492715205 (2026-09-28T22:29Z), so it predates LCLI-753. Recent wedges: 39873358281 attempts 1 and 2 (96f362cf; job 120152888119 then 120160392681), 39857558436 (6ff69788), 39433868424 (3aa5f020), 39360965506 (85d583c8), 37849280452, 37673274449, 37509680700, 37503495906, 36543946885, 36506568128, 36501610178, 36492715205. Same-SHA contrast: run 39857554409 at 6ff69788, started 2 s from the wedged 39857558436, passed macOS in ~8 min. SIGNATURE (leader): last (pass) line 2-18 s after the step starts, then ~19.5 min of silence until "The operation was canceled."; the last test differs each time (a runCheck case in three wedges, jobs 120152888119, 120099617794, 118665643969; a release.yml LCLI-621 case in 39873358281 attempt 2); --timeout=10000 never fires, so the bun process itself goes silent; cleanup reports "Terminate orphan process: pid (3654) (bun)". CONFIG: macos-latest falls through to ci.yml else branch `bun test --isolate --timeout=10000` with no outer timeout and no hung-only retry; ubuntu-latest bounds the same class of wedge with `timeout --kill-after=10s 6m` plus the LCLI-659 classifier retry. COVERAGE: macOS does not run on PRs (ci.yml matrix), so it is seen only after promotion. NOT COVERED by LCLI-753 (#654 bounded only the browser job install step) or LCLI-759 (browser job apt stall, a different job). acceptanceCriteria.text: DEC-236 clause 1a: the macos-latest Test step is bounded by an outer guard that ends a silent run well under the 20-minute job timeout (mechanism: scripts/run-hang-guarded.mjs, silence 120 s over a 14.9 s healthy maximum, wall backstop 660 s over a 579 s healthy maximum).

DEC-236 clause 1b: a HUNG run (guard exit 124) or a run whose every failing test hung at the per-test budget (scripts/ci-flake-classify.sh, LCLI-659) is retried exactly once; the green after it is labelled RETRY-GREEN as a ::warning:: annotation.
DEC-236 clause 1c: a real test failure fails the job with no retry, and a run that is still printing past the wall backstop (exit 125) is not retried either.

DEC-236 clause 2: on a hang the guard prints a process table and a macOS `sample` of every bun in the process group into the job log BEFORE killing it; positive control: the log shows a bun call graph, not an empty or no-such-process result.

DEC-236 proof, both ways, on macos-latest itself (workflow_dispatch of ci.yml on a scratch ref, stubs as real bun test files): a hanging stub is killed, sampled and retried once and the job is green with RETRY-GREEN; a second hang fails the job; a failing test fails with exactly one attempt; a clean pass has no retry. MEASUREMENTS 2026-10-23 behind the numbers (28 successful macOS jobs on the last 40 main-push CI runs, logs read): Test step 283-579 s, median 428 s; pre-Test steps 11-36 s; LARGEST gap between consecutive log lines inside the Test step 14.9 s (every job 5087+ lines). So a wall-clock cap alone cannot bound the wedge: two attempts at any cap above 579 s overrun the 20-minute job. Silence is the wedge signature, hence silence 120 s (8x the healthy maximum) with a 660 s wall backstop, 125 not retried. Budget: hang-then-pass ~36 + <=150 + 579 = ~765 s; hang-twice red after ~2 x 150 s; attempt 2 wall is clipped to a 1100 s job budget.

REVIEW VERDICT for opum-ai/lore-cli#662 at 1452062e, recorded VERBATIM from /Volumes/external/repos/opum-agent/scratchpad/lore-cli-review-662-verdict.txt (8777 bytes, sha256 6b125740f54f191ddc3b9204acfa123cb4430f4f3dc276f83ced75a9571ad1bf), Sonnet unit lore-cli-review-662:

VERDICT: APPROVE

Read-only review of opum-ai/lore-cli#662 at 1452062e. I read the code only. I ran nothing, and I could not fetch the run ids. I found no blocker. Findings are ordered by severity, and none of them block landing.

1. MEDIUM, not blocking. scripts/run-hang-guarded.mjs:159 settles on `close`, which waits for the stdio pipes to reach EOF, not on `exit`.
   - Scenario: bun exits on its own (status 0 or 1), but a leaked grandchild still holds the stdout or stderr fd. `close` never fires, and the watchdog (:129-133) sees silence and sets verdict "silent" after 120 s. The guard then exits 124. ci.yml retries on 124 without looking at the log (:373). A real failure then becomes a retry, and a retry that passes becomes RETRY-GREEN. A clean pass becomes a spurious retry.
   - Impact: this masks a real failure only if attempt 2 passes, so it is limited to flaky failures. The old `| tee` pipeline had the same EOF hazard.
   - Suggested fix: record the child's `exit` code and, on `exit`, give the pipes a short grace period before settling with that code.
   - The same shape applies to a wedge that comes after real `(fail)` lines. That is a 124 and is retried, which is acceptable because a deterministic failure fails again on attempt 2.

2. LOW. The "<=150 s detect + sample + kill" budget (ci.yml:354, script header) assumes few bun processes. sampleGroup (:85-98) runs `sample pid 3` serially, with a 60 s cap each. With N buns in the group, sampling takes at least 3N seconds, and it blocks the event loop because it uses spawnSync. I could not see how many buns `--isolate` leaves in the group. For hang-twice, N is probably small, but "red at 4m09" shows N=1 only. Not verified for the real suite.

3. LOW. `finish()` (:152) sends SIGKILL to -pgid unconditionally, including after a normal exit. That is intended, since it reaps leftovers. The group is normally empty by then, so PID reuse is theoretical.
   - The guard installs no SIGTERM or SIGINT handler. If the runner cancels the job, the detached group is not killed by the guard. The runner's own orphan sweep covers this, as it did before.
   - A process in uninterruptible sleep after SIGKILL would hang `close` forever, and the watchdog is inert once a verdict is set (:130). The job timeout is the only backstop, and it is unlikely.

4. LOW. SECONDS (ci.yml:388) counts only from the start of the Test step. The "1100 s job budget" therefore assumes the pre-Test steps took 100 s or less. The measured pre-Test time was 11-36 s, so this is fine. The classifier path has a corner case: if attempt 1 takes about 579 s (the slowest healthy time) and then fails with all-hangs, attempt 2 gets about 521 s. A healthy attempt 2 near 579 s would then be killed at 125 and the job goes red. This requires a rare joint event, and it fails safe (red). Comment :356-357, "even the classifier arm cannot run into the job timeout", is true by construction but not by margin.

5. LOW. The test pins are string-contains checks on the workflow text, not behaviour.
   - test/ci-workflow.test.ts:184-205 would go red on a bare `bun test` at line start, on a third guarded call (`toHaveLength(2)`), on a missing 124/125/classifier/`exit "${lore_bun_status}"` string, on a missing RETRY-GREEN token, and on `continue-on-error` at job or Test-step level.
   - It would not catch `timeout 5 bun test` or `env bun test`, because the bare check anchors `^\s*bun test `.
   - It would not catch a retry added on a generic failure that keeps the old strings in place. For example, a changed `elif` condition or an edited body of the 125 branch (:376-378, `exit 1`) would still pass. The 124/125/classifier strings are only pinned as present.
   - The real proof is the dispatch run, which the repo does not re-run. This is adequate for a pin, but it is a pin and not a proof.
   - The added job-level `continue-on-error` type key (:17, :25) is harmless. It does overlap LCLI-758, so expect a trivial merge if that lands first.

6. INFO. The macOS positive control (test/run-hang-guarded.test.ts:145-164) is sound.
   - It runs bun under the guard with an Atomics.wait hang, and asserts 124, "bun processes in the group: 1", the sample header, and "Call graph:". A failed `sample` or a no-such-process result would fail it.
   - It is skipped on non-darwin via `skipIf`, and the other tests still run on Linux. A skipped test is reported as skipped, not as green.
   - macOS does not run on PRs, so this control only runs after promotion or under dispatch.
   - The silence, 125 and grandchild tests each take about 3 s under bun's `--timeout=10000`. They are fine when idle, but they add a little flake surface on a loaded macOS runner. A flake there would go through the classifier retry.

Answers to A-F:

A. Silence is tracked on both stdout and stderr (:126-127), on pipes the guard reads itself.
   - bun was already writing to a pipe under `| tee`, so buffering behaviour is the same as the measured logs.
   - A healthy burst after a quiet period can only be killed if the quiet exceeds 120 s. Per-test budgets are 10 s, and the measured maximum gap is 14.9 s, so 120 s is about 8x margin. That is justified by the data, but the data is the leader's, from 28 jobs, and I did not re-measure it.
   - Tests with explicit long timeouts, such as the new 90 s one, still print between tests.

B. The child is spawned `detached`, so it leads its own process group. The kill is `process.kill(-pgid)`: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 10 s, then SIGKILL again in `finish`. A child that ignores SIGTERM is covered.
   - The grandchild-kill test covers the group kill.
   - Exit 124 always follows a kill attempt, because the verdict is set immediately before sampling and the kill. An exit 124 with no kill is not possible.
   - A failed or absent `sample` is only logged (:90-96). The exit code is unaffected, and sampleGroup never throws.
   - Orphan and self-hang edges are in finding 3.

C. Exit codes:
   - A real failure surfaces as 124 only if the process goes silent for 120 s or its pipe stays open (finding 1). That is a hang-like case, and failures then recur on attempt 2.
   - The guard's own status is passed through, with 128+n for signals (:162-163). One test covers 143.
   - A spawn error is 127, and a usage error is 2.
   - 124 and 125 collide with the command's own status only if bun itself returns them, which it does not.
   - A 127 reaches the classifier, which exits 1 when it finds no failures (ci-flake-classify.sh:76). The job then ends `exit 127`, red with no retry.

D. The ci.yml arm (:358-399) reads correctly.
   - `set +e`, the `PIPESTATUS[0]` capture and `set -e` are the same as the ubuntu arm. bash 3.2 supports all of it.
   - The classifier call sits in an `elif` condition, so `set -e` does not fire on it.
   - Retry fires only on 124 or on classifier exit 0. 125 gives `exit 1`. Anything else gives `exit "${lore_bun_status}"`.
   - Attempt 2 is `if ! node ...`, then `exit 1`.
   - RETRY-GREEN is emitted only after a passing attempt 2.
   - The clip is `min(1100-SECONDS, 660)` with a floor check, which is arithmetically correct (see finding 4 for the margin).
   - No `|| true` and no continue-on-error. Attempt 2 is not teed to the log, which is harmless.

E. See findings 5 and 6.

F. Acceptance criteria at this head:
   - AC0 (1a bound): met. 120 s silence with a 660 s backstop is implemented and pinned.
   - AC1 (1b hung-only retry once, RETRY-GREEN as a ::warning::): met.
   - AC2 (1c real failure not retried, 125 not retried): met by construction. See finding 1 for the edge.
   - AC3 (process table and sample before the kill, with a positive control): met in code and test. The bun call graph on a real wedge is not proven here.
   - AC4 (proof both ways on macos-latest): code supports it. Run 39883110491 is claimed but I cannot verify it. Whether the record cites it is a task-finalization matter. The AC checkboxes are unchecked at this head.
   - AC5 (full suite on the final head, run id and duration cited): depends on run 39883131395 and 319 s. Unverifiable by me, and the cited run's head must equal the final PR head. The leader said all PR checks are green, but macOS does not run on PRs, so the dispatch run is the only macOS evidence.
   - AC6 (note each RETRY-GREEN on LCLI-760 with its sample): a process duty, not code. It is not testable at this head. The ci.yml message at :398 does point to it.

What I could NOT verify:
- The CI run ids, the macOS `sample` permissions on the runner, and the 28-job measurements.
- Whether `bun test --isolate` leaves multiple bun processes in the group.
- Whether any lore test leaks a pipe-holding grandchild, which is finding 1's trigger.
- That scripts/run-bounded.mjs is untouched. I did not diff it.
